## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--wait` alias needs fixing before merge. The ADR added in this pull request says `--wait` stays accepted for one release with a deprecation warning, but the parser drops it completely. Any existing invocation that passes `--wait` will now exit with an argparse error. The renamed option, the unchanged 30-second default and the unchanged format choices match the description and the tests.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Calling `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with status 2 ("unrecognized arguments"), when it should be accepted as a deprecated alias. The diff replaces `parser.add_argument("--wait", ...)` with `parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=30)` and registers no alias. That contradicts `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5`: "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." A search of the repository finds no other handling of `--wait`. To fix this, register `--wait` as a hidden alias that writes to `dest="timeout"`, for example with `help=argparse.SUPPRESS` or a custom action. Emit a `DeprecationWarning` or stderr message when it is used, and add tests that check `--wait 12` gives `args.timeout == 12` and that the warning fires. — Existing scripts and automation that pass `--wait` stop working immediately instead of getting the one-release deprecation period the ADR promises.

## Strengths
- The tests were updated consistently for the new flag. They cover the default (`args.timeout == 30`), an explicit value, and both invalid-input cases (`--timeout bad`, `--timeout` with no value), all of which still exit with code 2.
- The default and the `--format` choices are unchanged, as the PR body and the ADR's "Defaults" section state.
